AUDIT COMPLETE. Answer to the literal question: no - across 54 recorded runs in gather, reach never flipped a verdict (43 pass/warranted, 9 partial/warranted, 1 pass/insufficient, 1 pass/overkill; 50 of 54 had unreached files and none changed the outcome).

But that evidence does NOT justify the cut, because it measures a broken version of the metric. 53 of the 54 runs are harness 0.7.0/0.8.0 and predate the test_scripts exclusion (test_scripts key ABSENT in every one). In those runs test/unit/*.gd and devtools_ext/commands.gd dominate the unreached lists - up to 11 of 19 files in a single run - both of which the harness now correctly excuses. So the historical reach ratios are systematically depressed by a bug that is already fixed.

Post-fix sample size is n=1 (harness 0.10.0, 2026-08-06), and even that run mis-scores 4 of its 7 unreached files as headless-only tooling -> filed as its own bug.

VERDICT: do not cut verify_ledger.py. The metric has never actually been evaluated in its fixed form. Fix the remaining false-miss class first, then re-evaluate once there are post-fix runs to read. Cutting a metric on evidence gathered from its broken version is the wrong inference.

WONTFIX - already considered and rejected by this repo, on better grounds than the recommendation that reopened it. log-devtools.md (0.12.0 session, 'Considered and rejected this turn'): '4,172 lines in one file is the thing most likely to hurt later, and it is still not worth a refactor that has to preserve every _handlers registration exactly. The plugin's value is being trustworthy. Revisit with a concrete reason, not a line count.'

My recommendation was a line count. Looking for a concrete reason turned up none: the file is cleanly sectioned, every verb is greppable as _cmd_<verb>, CLAUDE.md already tells readers how to navigate it, and the log records no session that lost time to its size. Against that, a split introduces the Callable-lifetime hazard that already bit this repo once via _extension (a group object the core stops referencing frees every verb in it), across the 45-verb wire contract the repo names as its risk surface.

Reopen only with evidence of real cost - a session that actually lost time, or a merge conflict that a split would have avoided.

Fixed in 0.16.0. Reproduced first (H-033): step_time 5s + a ping 1s later produced the ping reply at 1.26s inside the step, overwritten at 5.12s. Fix is a _dispatch_busy guard checked at the top of _check_for_commands, before the read and the delete, so a mid-await command stays on disk and runs one tick after the handler returns; plus a 300s watchdog so a handler killed by a runtime error inside an await (which never resumes) cannot leave the bus permanently deaf. The guard also required a client-side change: devtools.py's 2s liveness precheck read 'command file still on disk' as proof nothing is polling, which a deferred command now contradicts, so it also requires no handler in flight (breadcrumb + fresh owner heartbeat). check_templates.py gained two stage-5 checks, both confirmed to fail first in all three ways (guard removed / guard after the read / client precheck reverted).

Fixed in 0.27.0 via a third path, stronger than either proposed fix: name_check.py --require-compile FILE shells one 'godot --check-only --script' per named file - verified read-only against .godot/ (no import, no cache write, safe concurrent), needs the project imported once already or a cross-file class_name false-positives. Directly reproduces and catches this bead's own regression case: 'extends RefCounted / func probe(b: Basis) -> Vector3: return b.get_column(0)' -> SCRIPT ERROR: Cannot find member get_column in base Basis, exit 1. A real compile catches this and any other member-not-found on a builtin, which is strictly more than option (a)'s builtin-locals lookup would have covered, without needing a third-party parser (option b). See log-devtools.md 2026-08-16 entry and gh#20.1 / plant-tower-defense:G-025 (same underlying ask, same fix).

Fixed in 0.29.0 (gh#30 / plant-tower-defense:G-014): a third path neither previous investigation considered - a self-report API. DevTools.mark_script_reached(path) lets a script that structurally can never be a node's script property (a static-utility class, or one loaded/called without ever being parented - this bead's own scene_validator.gd case) write its own path directly into the same _scripts_seen dict scripts-seen already reports and reach already reads. No engine-side load hook needed, no heuristic node/host mapping - the script calls it once from each real entry point. Modeled on the existing register_status_provider pattern. Mutation-tested (forcing the write to no-op correctly failed the new check_mark_script_reached control). Project code, including scene_validator.gd itself, needs one added call site to actually benefit - the harness side is done.
